This page checks the two Quarto *content* features that survive `minimal: true`
with their classes intact: column layouts and cross-references. It deliberately
contains no executable cells, so it carries no `_freeze/` entry and its prose
can be edited freely — see the note on frozen fixtures in `AUTHORING.md`.

Callouts are absent on purpose. Quarto only emits callout markup when Bootstrap
is loaded, so under `minimal: true` a callout div degrades to a blockquote with
its type discarded, and publication prep rejects the syntax outright.

## Column layouts

Body text sits at the reading measure, which is where prose belongs.

::: {.column-page}
This block carries `.column-page`. It should break out past the reading measure
while staying inside the page chrome, and it should stop breaking out entirely
once the window is too narrow to afford it.
:::

::: {.column-screen-inset}
This block carries `.column-screen-inset` and should be wider still, bounded by
the same rule: never wider than the room actually available.
:::

::: {.column-margin}
Margin content renders as an inset aside at reading width rather than a true
sidenote, because the right margin on this site belongs to the table of
contents.
:::

## Cross-references {#sec-crossrefs}

Cross-references are pure markup, so this page keeps them that way: no image
file and no executable cell, which is what lets the fixture stay unfrozen.

| basis | coefficients | energy retained |
|---|---|---|
| standard | 4,096 | 100% |
| Fourier | 17 | 94.6% |

: A table carrying a label, so pandoc numbers it. {#tbl-crossref}

The reference in this sentence points at @tbl-crossref, and this one points at
@sec-crossrefs. Pandoc numbers and links both without any help from Bootstrap,
which is why cross-references survive `minimal: true` when callouts do not.
